newsitem.title: UK: UK to require Plcs to publish bill-paying record.
newsitem.headline: UK to require Plcs to publish bill-paying record.

text.p: The government, in an effort to deter late payment, said on Friday it would require all public limited companies to disclose how long they take on average to pay their bills.
The annual requirement will also apply to the Plcs' large private subsidiaries, small businesses minister Richard Page said in a written parliamentary answer.
Late payment is one of the main concerns perenially highlighted by small firms.
Page said the annual disclosure of payment performance should help small firms to monitor the record of larger companies with which they are considering doing business.
The opposition Labour party said it had been calling for just such a step for several years and promised to go further if it wins power.
"Small firms need tough action on late payment, including a statutory right to interest on the late payment of debt," Barbara Roche, the party's small business spokemsan, said.
She said a survey last year conducted by Grant Thornton showed that the average payment period had lengthened to 60 days from 58 in 1995.
"This government has dithered and dodged the issue. The next Labour government will tackle it head on so that small firms get a fair deal," Roche added.
